> I’m building a custom alarm clock that wakes you up kindly. It uses an ESP32-C3 chip, a 2.4-inch color screen, a buzzer, and four buttons, all on a PCB I designed myself  The clock gets the exact time from WiFi and shows it with the date all day. At 7:30 AM it rings gently, and after you stop it, the screen shows a positive affirmation and a manifestation for the day. At 9 PM it shows a calming evening message. You can set the alarm directly on the clock, so it’s both a useful alarm and a small daily dose of positivity.

## Design

### 2026-11-08: yahh entry 1

**4.48h**

yahh entry 1

I had multiple ideas this week.

First of all I wanted to make an idea box where I can just record my ideas with a microphone and a battery and I can also relisten to my own ideas.  with the help of AI, use my own ideas. AI also looks at all my ideas and makes a list of my ideas: where they can go, how they can go, and how they can perform. This is because, as someone, I really get so many ideas in different sectors and sometimes I just forget my ideas.

First I wanted to make this. I was sure that I'm going to make this. Then for some reason I started scrolling Instagram and I saw a Hack North Hackathon video where they get this computer as a gift if they attend. It was a game console. Then I saw it and I was like, "You know what? I need this game console because it was so pretty. It was so good. I just want it now."

And then I decided to make a game console, switching from the idea of an idea box to a game console. A game console needs a lot of other stuff so I had to go through multiple videos on the internet. I'm watching how a game console actually works and how we can make one

I saw multiple videos and saw how to make this and all that stuff datasheets they cooked me fr. Then I saw which microcontroller I can use. I used ESP32 C3 for the idea box but the pins were getting less so I had to shift to ESP32 S3 WRM1n8r8. Then I added an audio amplifier and a display, which is an 8-pin display, and then I added 9 switches. 4 of the switches are useful for up, down, left, and right, and the A button and B button are for selecting options of the game on and off button start button

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 134316](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/k9cK7RFJqruSmBgZjJV0pElVN8uP2ZCX/aede90ab3dcd277c3dc18814a12e53243fc4e85f4cd6ab4078a4428929e642db.png)

Because I decided that I'll put multiple games with the SD card storage, whenever I make a game I can store that game and play that game in the game console of my own, which is going to be the best feeling. Yeah that's how I thought.

### 2026-11-08: I went. I already added ESP32 and switches and display. Then it was the time when I needed to work on the battery and the firmware.

**3.02h**

I went. I already added ESP32 and switches and display. Then it was the time when I needed to work on the battery and the firmware.

Actually the more I go into the depth of how I can make it exactly the way I wanted, the more components come up, like I wanted it the way I saw it there in the GX gadgets. It was so good, extremely, such a big big project and a good project. I'm thinking I was replicating it. I cannot use AI and nobody's there to guide me. At this point in time I was cooked because I was so confused. There are like 48 pins overall and I know that pins 19 and 20 are the pins which I need to connect to the USB. There are also a lot of other pins when I'm trying to connect USB and there are also resistors. For every other part there is so much work.

Since I have got into that thing to do, I've realized that the components keep on adding and I don't have that much of an idea as well. I was cooked at this point, really, I'm telling you. It was like Friday evening. I started the project on Thursday evening and it's festival time for me here in India. It's Diwali.

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 230747](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/k9cK7RFJqruSmBgZjJV0pElVN8uP2ZCX/8a5ad5659bc63b6c5bf524321bb47630f1478007ea8f07a354741c6d53d00ef5.png)

I realized that if I continue on the game console itself, the project is not going to get submitted. I'm not going to submit the project, the deadline will be passed, and I will be off life because I worked really hard for 4 weeks. I cannot just dismantle it for just 1 week for that one game console.

Then I just changed the plan from the game console to an alarm clock. Since I already worked with ESP32 C3 and the display, I changed the display from a normal one to an OLED to TFT because I've not worked with TFT. I wanted something new to work with so I worked with a TFT display and the buzzer is the same. Then I added all these components and then I just assigned the footprints for them, which was also very simple because I already worked with them.

### 2026-11-08: 1. I updated the schematic from schematic editor to PCB editor and then I did the routing.

**3.95h**

1. I updated the schematic from schematic editor to PCB editor and then I did the routing.
2. I added the 3D models.
3. I added the edge cut layer.
4. I added the GND layer for the F copper layer. I'm done with that.
Then I shifted to firmware. As per my idea, which you can see in my GitHub repo, I wanted to add affirmations and manifestation. It is kind of something that I have heard about recently through some of my favorite actors and I really wanted to try it if that is really true or not. I have been trying to integrate it into my routine for a very long time but I was unable to do so. I think this was the time to add it.
1. I did the firmware. I lapsed just for  30   min
2. I pushed the code to GitHub.
3. I wrote the readme.
4. I pushed the code to GitHub and I'm done with the project.
Finally I'm just submitting the project and I'm going to celebrate my festival peacefully right now. It's Diwali, the festival of lights
